newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH RESULT "AWFUL" BUT EXPECTED -ANALYST.
newsitem.headline: CHH RESULT "AWFUL" BUT EXPECTED -ANALYST.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd's first quarter profit of NZ$49 million was "awful" but expected, Doyle Paterson Brown analyst David Stanley said.
The result compared to analysts' range of forecasts of NZ$45-50 million and the June quarter 1996 profit of $56 million.
"These are tough times. One can't get around the fact that the returns generated at the moment are still well below what analysts would like or CHH itself would like to see.
"You could not describe it as a good result and they are certainly not saying that. It was an awful result really, but expected, by and large," Stanley told Reuters.
In the near term, conditions in New Zealand were likely to remain difficult.
"Exporters will be assisted by the lower New Zealand dollar, but it is clear that the domestic economy is still very weak and likely to remain so for the rest of this calendar year."
But Stanley said CHH should report successively better numbers as the company progresses through the financial year.

Analysts started revising down their expectations about a month ago to around NZ$275 million from an earlier forecast of $300 million compared with an actual outcome of NZ$251 million in the year to March, 1997.
"Its really a question of where to from here, and most of it is on the up from here," Stanley said.
Chief executive John Faraci was mildly confident that pulp price increases were sustainable.
"We are are looking positively at pulp and paper prices but with cautious optimism. I would be wary of pulp prices rising too quickly," Stanley said.
